utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Brdjanin, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner, Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager, Your Honours, good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you. Any news about --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we haven't heard anything, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Barbara Baruch assisted by Aleksandar Vujic for the defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman is all right?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: He's okay, Your Honour, thank you for asking. I had a few things when you had a second. Shall I bring them up now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to be in open session or in private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Open session is fine. Yesterday I offered two exhibits and I did not say under seal, and it concerned me afterwards to make sure that it would be under --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. It's nice of you and very considerate of you, Mrs. Baruch. They will be -- they are already under seal, actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Good. Okay the second thing is I need to announce that we still haven't heard anything from the American embassy, and of course if this Court orders that somebody from the Defence come tomorrow, we would not permit ourselves to be held in contempt. However, we also do not want to be felons. I appreciate that this Court -- this Tribunal is working as hard as it can to assist us in that endeavour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will ask Mr. Ackerman to choose between you and him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Okay. Can we send our daughter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for your observation and -- for your observation, Mrs. Baruch. All I know is that the President's office was very actively involved in the matter yesterday. I haven't -- believe me I haven't had the time this morning to consult with the President. I know that he was busy at half past 8.00 already, so I don't know what or if there are any developments at all. But probably if there will not be any developments, I may actually place an order because I'm pretty confident that this permit, if it doesn't arrive today, it will arrive tomorrow; and if doesn't arrive tomorrow it will arrive the day after. So if I do give an order it's because in my heart of heart convinced I will not be exposing you to any prejudice, danger at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I know that you would be my best witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one matter raise and I wonder if we could go into private session for it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By the way, Ms. Korner, the military expert is coming tomorrow, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we plan to finish with this witness today?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we try on Friday to finish a little bit earlier because I am replacing Judge Pocar on something important, and I need to leave The Hague at roughly 12.00 to 12.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll let Mr. Nicholls know, who is dealing with Mr. Brown. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, have you sorted out -- how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'll give them more than half the time. I don't think I'll take more than -- if we get started, I think I can finish in the first session, the direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you, Mrs. Baruch?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I don't know how these witnesses have been going. I've been reading the transcripts, Your Honour, and so long as we are not getting into the intercepted conversations at all but just about the witness, I think for sure we are going to be finished today and probably early as we were yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Anyway, I may as we go along have to impose a time limit. So let's start, Mr. Koumjian. We are in closed session, if I remember well, no.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We could be in open session for just the very beginning, before the witness comes in. I just would like to mark some documents before the witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment because I need --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, go slowly, Mr. Koumjian, because this area is pretty much complicated and I want to make sure that I am following 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: May I have just a moment? Okay. What I propose is -- Your Honour, is to introduce the intercepts themselves as two exhibits. First the group of intercepts containing the voice -- containing -- in which Mr. Brdjanin is one of the participants and this would also include one speech he gave. And I'd ask that that be marked people's next in order, which is P2382 -- excuse me, the next exhibit in order. That was an old habit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where do we find that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: This group of intercepts -- I'll go through them individually and I'd like each one to be marked .1, .2, et cetera, so that each one receives a separate exhibit number but all under P2382. The first would be a transcript of a phone conversation between Karadzic and Brdjanin dated the 17th of June, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 17th and 18th of June I have here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And just to be clear, the English translation transcript is 03076498.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I want to make sure that Mrs. Baruch is in a position to follow too.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I don't think I would be, Your Honour, because as I explained before he proceeded and I had discussions with Mr. Ackerman with regard to this, the transcripts, intercepts, had not been offered or discussed even during his cross-examination of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think you have understood me. All I want -- we are identifying the various transcripts and giving them an exhibit number. This is the exercise that I want to make sure that you can follow. You have a copy of all the transcripts. That I know for sure because we asked about that when we had the previous witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can give Ms. Baruch a list in order of the intercepts I'm offering. And just also to make clear to her, I do not intend to go into the content of the intercepts with the witness. The witness will simply talk about listening and recognising the voice.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I do understand that. I would like again the date, please, of that particular transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sure. Actually, I'll give you a spreadsheet. I can hand it to you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are talking, Mrs. Baruch, of a conversation between Radoslav Brdjanin and Radovan Karadzic conducted on 17/18 June, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I have a copy of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I do have a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So that will become P?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 2382.1. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Second would be a conversation, same participants, 2nd July, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 2nd and 3rd July, P2382.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: That one I don't believe that I have. The 2nd of July -- was that one -- oh, it had been mistranslated or something so that they had written 92 instead of 1991. But it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1992 I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If I give you the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's P2382.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: And just so that the Court would understand, what I had been saying is my understanding from Mr. Ackerman or the prior transcripts were -- was that he had previously been told and typed on that particular transcript, it says 2/3 July, 1992, but that was in error and it is actually a 1991 conversation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. You can see on the B/C/S transcript it says 1991 and on the English it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Listen, next can we do it in another fashion so that we -- you have a list, you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: With an exhibit number that you intend to give to each --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. You will put that into the record and we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, we don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- don't have to go and spend three-quarters of an hour going through each and every one of these transcripts. And in the course of your examination-in-chief, you will just refer to the exhibit number and we look at the chart or at the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If Your Honour wants I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because otherwise, Mr. Koumjian, it's going to take us an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, I could just simply read the ERN numbers and we can go through them or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't need to, just file it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Give us a copy --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We will be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I don't know if we have a copy. I don't think -- yes, my apologies to the interpreters. I am talking too fast. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can we move into evidence or move to have marked as an exhibit at this time. I understand the Court has reserved its ruling, P2382.1 through.14. Those are the bundle of conversations in which Mr. Brdjanin appears. And secondly, as the next exhibit in order P2383.1 through .16, 16 separate intercepts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically if I read you well, the first group, the P2382 series are intercepts of telephone conversations in which you allege -- stands to be proved, that Mr. Brdjanin was one of the persons on line being intercepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Correct, with the exception of .14, which is a speech given at the Holiday Inn I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: With the exception of .14. And the others are intercepts of conversations between other personalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, with the exception that again there are one speeches by Mr. -- there is one speech by Mr. Karadzic contained in two of the -- .14 and .15 are speeches by Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to help Your Honours on the spreadsheet, the point numbers are on the right. The tab numbers I don't believe will help Your Honours. That was from our internal collection, the left-hand column. Just the right-hand column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think we can proceed along this way and we'll probably cut down considerably on the time. We need a copy of that, Mr. Koumjian, because I don't -- ah, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is not what he has in his hands. My eyesight is still good enough to see that he is not reading from the same document that I have in front of me. May have given it to us yesterday, I don't know, but -- you see, that's different. Yes. This we have. Yeah, yeah yeah, but this is not what we had earlier on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, I think that's clear enough, Mr. Koumjian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we can -- are you happy, Mrs. Baruch?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I'm not happy, but yes, I have these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. We can call in the witness and go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, unfortunately I have to bring you some bad news, members of the public, or the audience. We have to go into closed session and therefore, as starting from now, you will not be able to follow the remaining part of the proceedings. I'm sorry about that but it's part of our rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: May I just ask, if that has anything to do with the admission of any of these exhibits, could -- if you make your motion now, I can go and relate it to Mr. Ackerman but you could make it directly while he is here, because I believe he will be here tomorrow morning. So that's up to you, and the Tribunal, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what Mr. Koumjian is going to say. So yes, Mr. Koumjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It might be helpful to everyone if Ms. Gustin has put the exhibit numbers on -- annex A of the last witness's statement he went through a series of the tapes and what he recognised, it might be helpful to Your Honours to put the exhibit numbers. For the first nine it's actually in order, P2382 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's start with 2.330 would be what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: .1 and then the next is .2, .3, the first page is in order, .1, .2, .3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't understand either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 238 -- this is already P2385.1. This document itself annex A is P2385.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Right. So what I'm just saying -- the particular tapes that the witness listened to starting with the first one, which is on the left-hand column it's labelled by the disclosure number, 233, that intercept is labelled -- has been marked as an Exhibit P2382.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this is P2382.1, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Next is 2382.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a reference chart -- becomes a reference chart. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It's in order. The first two pages are exactly in order through the first eight intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: .3 and then the next page .4, .5, through .8. Going to the third page, whenever Your Honours are ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The first is 2832 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to make sure that Mrs. Baruch is following.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I'm following exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the next one is 2349, 2349 becomes -- is

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 2382.9, then we go out of the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 2382.9. And we continue --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 2382.12 is the second one down. The third one, as indicated in the comments --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The second one, 2.351 is P2382. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The next one --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The third one as pointed out in the comments is the same as an earlier one, so it's a duplicate of P2382.3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And the last one on this page is P2382.14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Going to the fourth page, they are P2382.10 and .11 in that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Going to the fifth page, the first one was previously marked as an exhibit during Mr. Treanor's I believe, testimony, that's P2357.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 2357, correct. The middle one is P2383.11, .11. The last one on page 5, and the remaining two on the next page are not offered into evidence. They are not exhibits in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's very useful indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And one other brief point I'd like to bring out to Your Honours, in reference to the motion on the admissibility of the legality, on the Exhibit 2382.7, that intercept, you will hear Mr. Brdjanin make a statement that his phone is tapped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He said it's on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. And on the next exhibit, 2383.9, Mr. Karadzic tells Vojo Kupresanin that Mr. Karadzic says his phone is tapped. Obviously we point that out to show that there was not an expectation of privacy on those intercepts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I've gone through the intercepts already, Mr. Koumjian, and I'm pretty much aware that there was this, at least from what they show on the face of it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, that's all from me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mrs. Baruch, anything else before we go to leave?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I don't believe so, but if I'm expected to return with an answer to something, if you give me a clue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. What is important is that tomorrow you come back with a feedback on what we discussed earlier on today, that's all, feedback from Mr. Ackerman -- or Mr. Ackerman I understand will be here himself. So the sitting stands adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Tomorrow is the military expert. Tomorrow is the military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So we will not discuss the legality of the intercepts tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, if Mr. Ackerman had been here, I would have asked you both to go into it and discuss it. What I can do -- I mean, I'm not going anywhere now. If Mr. Ackerman can come forward and have submissions, make submissions, we could do that. We can break for 25 minutes and then we'll see if he's in a position to come over, but I pretty much doubt it. On the other hand the other alternative is to let you make submissions, but then does it make sense?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No. I just wanted to know whether to be here tomorrow or not. One other housekeeping matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think both Judge Janu and Judge Taya and myself are available if we can accommodate you, we will, and if we can find a way of dealing with this matter today, we would rather have it done today than postpone it. Do you think it's possible for Mr. Ackerman to come over?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Judge. I'm sorry, I can't answer for that. If I were to guess from this morning, I would say no, but if you'd like, he can certainly call the Office of the Prosecutor and if he's able to do it today, then the Court -- the Tribunal would be notified. Okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do this, Mr. Koumjian: I will break now, we will break now, try to contact Mr. Ackerman, see if you can reach an agreement on this, whether he would be prepared, for example, to have you submit oral pleadings in his absence now and in the presence of Mrs. Baruch, of course, and then he will respond some other time. I don't know. I mean, that's why I said we will accommodate you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll call him immediately after court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And contact Madam Chuqing, who will then contact me so that we will be in a position to know. If you can do that, as early, as soon as possible, at least you won't keep everyone waiting here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I do recall he indicated he wanted to file additional written response but I'll call him find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it's up to you. I mean, we don't really interfere much in these matters. We try to make your life easy or easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm prepared to rule if it's up to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I would rule as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, in reference to the statement that Ms. Korner mentioned in private session at the beginning of today, to provide to Your Honours, I have three copies to provide to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that the other copy has been redacted and will be handed over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The redacted version is not ready yet to be given to the Defence. That will be provided by the end of the day to the Defence in redacted form.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: By bicycle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So for the time being, unless we have news that we will be reconvening, we stand adjourned. And if we stand adjourned, that will be until tomorrow morning at 9.00, with the understanding that the whole morning will be dedicated to the military expert. All right? Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 10th day of July, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.46 a.m.,
